text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today, but that gain masks a sharp two-week decline of over 8% that accelerated after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th. The stock has been under pressure as crude oil prices have fallen—Brent crude dipped below $90 a barrel on Monday after President Trump suggested the Iran conflict would "end fairly soon," reducing concerns about Middle East supply disruptions that had been supporting energy prices. With fewer geopolitical risks to oil markets, crude has retreated from higher levels, which directly weighs on the economics of oil producers like ConocoPhillips.

The stock's weakness also reflects the narrow margin oil majors face right now: while US crude sits around $99 per barrel, the gap between US and global prices (Brent at $107) has tightened considerably. For a company that sells into global markets, a lower oil price environment—whether driven by peace hopes or simply reduced supply anxiety—cuts into profit margins and makes the business less attractive to investors, especially after the company just reported its quarterly results.
